questions.q: Solid rectangular beam section of area A carries transverse shear V. Peak transverse shear stress and its location?
questions.x: τ = VQ/(Ib) is parabolic through the depth, zero at the free top and bottom faces and peaking at 1.5 times the average V/A on the neutral axis, where Q is largest.

questions.q: Rectangle b × h carries a compressive axial load at eccentricity e along the depth h. The whole section stays in compression when:
questions.a: e ≤ h/6 (load within the middle third)
questions.x: The fiber stress P/A − Pe(h/2)/I reaches zero at e = I/(A·h/2) = h/6, so a load inside the middle third (the kern) keeps every fiber compressive.

questions.q: A rectangular beam keeps its width b and moment M, but its depth h is doubled. Peak bending stress changes by a factor of:
questions.x: The section modulus S = bh²/6 grows with h², so σ_max = M/S drops to one quarter; the bending stiffness EI grows eightfold with h³.

questions.q: Along a transversely loaded beam, the bending moment reaches a local extreme where:
questions.a: The shear force V passes through zero
questions.x: Moment equilibrium of a beam element gives dM/dx = V, so M is stationary where V = 0, and the shear diagram crossing zero marks the peak moment.

questions.q: Solid circular shaft, diameter 50 mm, bending moment 1.5 kN·m. Maximum bending stress in MPa (1 decimal)?
questions.x: With I = πd⁴/64 and c = d/2, σ_max = 32M/(πd³) = 32(1.5×10⁶)/(π·50³) ≈ 122.2 MPa.

questions.q: Complete the elastic section modulus of a b × h rectangle (bending about the axis parallel to b)
questions.x: I = bh³/12 and c = h/2, so S = bh²/6 and σ_max = M/S.

questions.q: Match each wing load to the deformation it mainly drives
pairs: Lift acting off the shear center
questions.x: Each load drives the mode whose stiffness resists it: lift bends flapwise, drag bends chordwise, a lift offset from the shear center twists, and inertia loads on the wing reduce root bending.

questions.q: Uniform Euler-Bernoulli cantilever, mass per length m. First bending natural frequency?
questions.x: The cantilever frequency equation cos βL cosh βL = −1 has lowest root βL ≈ 1.875, giving ω₁ ≈ 3.52 √(EI/(mL⁴)).

questions.q: Thin-walled open section whose straight walls all meet at one point (an angle or a T). Shear center?
questions.a: At the point where the walls meet
w: Outside the section on the heel side
At the midpoint of the longest wall
questions.x: Each wall's shear flow resultant acts along that wall, so every resultant passes through the common junction, which is therefore the shear center.

questions.q: Closed thin circular tube, midline radius 50 mm, wall 2 mm, torque 3 kN·m. Shear stress by Bredt, in MPa (1 decimal)?
questions.x: τ = T/(2At) with enclosed area A = πR² = 7854 mm², so τ = 3×10⁶/(2·7854·2) ≈ 95.5 MPa.

questions.q: Complete the torsion constant of a single closed thin-walled cell (enclosed area A)
questions.x: Bredt gives q = T/(2A) and twist rate θ' = T∮(ds/t)/(4A²G) = T/(GJ), so J = 4A²/∮(ds/t); a circular tube gives J = 2πR³t.

questions.q: Single closed thin cell of varying wall thickness under pure torque. The shear flow and shear stress are:
questions.a: q constant around the cell, τ = q/t largest where the wall is thinnest
w: τ constant around the cell, q largest where the wall is thickest
q largest at the thickest wall
q proportional to the distance from the centroid
questions.x: Axial equilibrium of a wall element makes dq/ds = 0 in pure torsion, so q = T/(2A) everywhere and the thinnest wall sees the peak stress.

questions.q: A torque tube has two segments of different GJ along its span and carries the same torque T through both. Total twist?
w: Torques add and both segments share one twist
questions.x: Segments along the span act in series: each carries the full torque and their torsional compliances L/(GJ) add.

questions.q: Thin channel under vertical shear through its shear center. Shape of the shear flow distribution?
questions.a: Linear in the flanges, parabolic in the web
w: Parabolic in the flanges, linear in the web
questions.x: In a flange y is constant, so Q = ∫ y t ds grows linearly with s; in the web y varies linearly, so Q and hence q grow quadratically, peaking at the neutral axis.

questions.q: Match each section to its torsion constant J
pairs: Closed thin tube, radius R, wall t
Closed thin equilateral triangle, side c, wall t
questions.x: Solid circles use the polar moment, closed cells use Bredt 4A²/∮ds/t, and open walls use Σbt³/3.

questions.q: Two-cell closed section under torque, cell shear flows q₁ and q₂ (same sense). Shear flow in the shared web?
w: Zero, the web is idle in torsion
questions.x: Shear flow continuity at each web junction makes the shared wall carry the difference of the two adjacent cell flows.

questions.q: A linear elastic structure carries load P that is raised slowly from zero, giving deflection Δ along P. Strain energy stored?
questions.x: Clapeyron's theorem: for linear response the load grows in proportion to Δ, so the work done is the triangle area ½PΔ, stored as strain energy.

questions.q: Castigliano's first theorem (strain energy U written in terms of displacements) states:
questions.x: The first theorem gives the force at a point as the derivative of U(Δ) with respect to the displacement there, and it holds for nonlinear elastic materials too.

questions.q: An approximate solution from minimum complementary energy (assumed statically admissible stresses) gives a structural stiffness that is:
questions.a: Too low, a lower bound on stiffness
w: Too high, an upper bound on stiffness
Exact for any admissible stress field
Too high for loads and too low for moments
questions.x: Assumed stresses overestimate the complementary energy, so deflections come out large and stiffness low, which brackets the exact answer from below while assumed displacements bracket it from above.

questions.q: Reduction theorem: to find a deflection of an indeterminate structure by the unit load method, the virtual unit load may be applied to:
questions.a: Any statically determinate released version of the structure
w: The released structure with the redundants set to zero in the real moments
A mechanism formed by removing all supports
questions.x: The real moments M come from the full solution, while the virtual moments m need only equilibrium, so any stable determinate release gives the same deflection with far less work.

questions.q: Cantilever, L = 1000 mm, EI = 10¹¹ N·mm², tip moment M₀ = 2 kN·m. Tip deflection by the unit load method, in mm?
questions.x: M = M₀ along the span and a unit tip load gives m = (L − x), so Δ = ∫M₀(L − x)dx/EI = M₀L²/(2EI) = 10 mm.

questions.q: Complete the strain energy of a uniform shaft of length L under torque T
questions.x: Torsion stores U = ∫T²/(2GJ) dx, the companion of N²L/(2EA) for axial load and ∫M²/(2EI) dx for bending.

questions.q: Put the Rayleigh-Ritz steps for a beam in order
steps: Choose trial functions that satisfy the essential (kinematic) boundary conditions
Write Π(a₁, …, a_n) = U − W, including any spring energies
Solve the linear system for a_i and recover deflections and moments
questions.x: Admissible trial functions make Π a function of the coefficients, and stationarity with respect to each a_i gives the best approximation within that family.

questions.q: Match each energy principle to what it states
pairs: Work of load set 1 on displacements of set 2 equals work of set 2 on set 1
U = ½ΣP_iΔ_i for a linear structure
questions.x: The two minimum principles are dual (displacements give equilibrium, stresses give compatibility), and Betti and Clapeyron follow from linearity.

questions.q: Rigid bar of length L pinned at its base, top spring k that stays horizontal (stretch L sin θ), vertical dead load P. Equilibrium gives P = kL cos θ. Post-buckling behavior?
questions.a: Unstable symmetric bifurcation, P falls with |θ|
w: Stable symmetric bifurcation, P rises with |θ|
questions.x: The path P = kL cos θ drops on both sides of P_cr = kL, so the critical state is unstable and the structure is imperfection sensitive with a two-thirds power knockdown.

questions.q: Asymmetric bifurcation with an imperfection of amplitude ε. The drop in maximum load scales as:
questions.x: A linear initial post-buckling slope (P/P_cr ≈ 1 + aθ) gives a knockdown proportional to √ε on the falling side, a half-power law that is even harsher than the two-thirds law of unstable symmetric systems.

questions.q: A dead load is applied suddenly (a step, then held) to an undamped linear elastic system. Peak deflection?
questions.x: Energy balance PΔ = ½kΔ² at the turning point gives Δ_max = 2P/k, so the system oscillates about the static position with an amplitude equal to it.

questions.q: Multi-DOF conservative system at an equilibrium. The equilibrium is stable when:
questions.a: The Hessian of Π is positive definite
w: The determinant of the Hessian is negative
Every entry of the Hessian is positive
questions.x: Stability means Π is a local minimum, so the second variation must be positive for every perturbation, which is positive definiteness of ∂²Π/∂q_i∂q_j; P_cr is where its lowest eigenvalue reaches zero.

questions.q: Rigid bar, L = 0.5 m, pinned base with rotational spring C = 2000 N·m, plus a top spring k = 4000 N/m that stays horizontal (stretch L sin θ). Vertical dead load P at the top. P_cr in N?
questions.x: Π = ½Cθ² + ½kL²sin²θ − PL(1 − cos θ), and the θ² coefficient vanishes at P_cr = C/L + kL = 4000 + 2000 = 6000 N, since both springs resist the same tilt.

questions.q: Complete the effect of axial compression on the fundamental frequency of a pinned-pinned column (ω₀ at zero load)
questions.x: The bending frequency squared falls linearly with compressive load and reaches zero at P_cr, which is the kinetic method's criterion for a conservative load.

questions.q: Match each stability method to its critical condition
pairs: The second variation of Π loses positive definiteness
A frequency drops to zero, or two frequencies coalesce (flutter)
Deflection grows unbounded as P approaches P_cr
questions.x: For conservative loads all four give the same P_cr; the kinetic method also handles follower loads, where instability can appear as flutter.

questions.q: Rigid bar, base spring C, dead load P, initial tilt θ₀ at zero spring moment (θ from the vertical). Imperfect equilibrium path?
questions.x: Π = ½C(θ − θ₀)² − PL(cos θ₀ − cos θ), and dΠ/dθ = 0 gives C(θ − θ₀) = PL sin θ, a path that starts at zero load at θ₀ and rises smoothly through the neighbourhood of P_cr = C/L.

questions.q: Plane pin-jointed truss with m members, r reaction components and j joints. Degree of static indeterminacy?
questions.x: Each joint gives two force equilibrium equations, so the unknowns m + r exceed the 2j equations by the degree of indeterminacy (for a stable truss).

questions.q: Two springs k₁ and k₂ act in parallel between the same two points. They share:
questions.a: The same displacement, and stiffnesses add
w: The same force, and stiffnesses add
The same force, and compliances add
The same displacement, and compliances add
questions.x: Parallel elements undergo one common deflection, so their forces add and k_eq = k₁ + k₂.

questions.q: An indeterminate structure includes a cable. The solution gives the cable a compressive force. Next step?
questions.a: Remove the cable as slack and re-solve the structure
w: Keep the compressive force, since compatibility holds
Halve the cable stiffness and iterate
Reverse the sign of the force and keep the solution
questions.x: A cable carries tension only, so a compressive result means it goes slack and the structure is re-solved with the cable removed.

questions.q: Force method with a member that is too short by δ (lack of fit) or heated by ΔT. The effect enters:
questions.a: As an initial displacement term in the compatibility equation
w: As a change in the flexibility coefficients f_ij
As an extra redundant force X₂ at the misfit member
questions.x: Compatibility becomes Δ₁₀ + f₁₁X₁ + Δ₁ᵢ = 0, where Δ₁ᵢ is the relative displacement across the release, positive in the X₁ sense, produced on the released structure by the misfit δ or the free thermal extension αΔT·L.

questions.q: Cantilever, L = 1000 mm, EI = 10¹¹ N·mm². A spring k = 600 N/mm hangs from the tip and a 1 kN load hangs from the spring. Deflection of the load point in mm?
questions.x: The tip stiffness 3EI/L³ = 300 N/mm acts in series with the 600 N/mm spring, so k_eq = 200 N/mm and the load point moves 1000/200 = 5 mm.

questions.q: Complete the clamp moment of a propped cantilever (fixed at A, roller at B) under uniform load w
questions.x: The roller reaction is 3wL/8, so M_A = wL²/2 − (3wL/8)L = wL²/8.

questions.q: Match each planar support to the reactions it supplies
pairs: One force normal to the rolling surface
questions.x: Each reaction corresponds to a restrained motion, so counting restrained translations and rotations gives r for the indeterminacy count.

questions.q: Put the displacement (stiffness) method steps in order
steps: Identify the unknown joint displacements and rotations
Write member end forces in terms of those displacements
Assemble joint equilibrium K d = F
Solve for d and recover the member forces
questions.x: The stiffness method takes displacements as unknowns, so compatibility holds by construction and equilibrium at the joints gives the equations.

questions.q: Rectangular curved beam, R/h = 10 (R to the centroid), pure bending. The straight-beam formula underestimates the inner-fiber stress by about:
questions.x: Winkler theory with r_n = h/ln(r_o/r_i) gives an inner-fiber stress about 1.035 times My/I at R/h = 10, so the straight formula is adequate for slender curvature.

questions.q: Two materials with volume fractions f₁ and f₂ form layers loaded side by side (equal strain). Effective axial modulus?
questions.a: E = f₁E₁ + f₂E₂, the Voigt upper bound
questions.x: Equal strain makes stresses add by area fraction, giving the rule of mixtures; stacking the layers in series (equal stress) gives the Reuss lower bound.

questions.q: A frame corner joint is semi-rigid (flexible). How is it modelled?
questions.a: A rotational spring k_θ: relative member rotation = M/k_θ
w: A linear spring along each member
A rigid joint with each member's EI halved
A pin carrying a moment equal to the applied load
questions.x: The joint rotational spring adds ½M²/k_θ to U and spans the range from a pin (k_θ → 0) to a rigid joint (k_θ → ∞).

questions.q: Semicircular two-hinged arch (pinned at both ends) under a crown load. Redundant usually chosen and how it is found?
w: Vertical reaction at one end, from ∂U/∂V = 0
Crown moment, from ∂U/∂M = 0 at the crown
Horizontal thrust H, from vertical equilibrium
questions.x: Vertical reactions follow from statics, leaving the horizontal thrust as the single redundant, fixed by least work since the supports stay a fixed distance apart.

questions.q: Sandwich beam: width 100 mm, face thickness 2 mm (thin), face centroid separation 20 mm, moment 1 kN·m. Face stress in MPa?
questions.x: The faces form a couple, so each face force is M/d = 50 kN over an area bt = 200 mm², giving σ_f = M/(btd) = 250 MPa.

questions.q: Complete the Winkler neutral axis radius of a curved beam of section area A
questions.x: Zero net force with hyperbolic stress gives r_n = A/∫dA/r, which lies between the centroid and the center of curvature; a rectangle gives r_n = h/ln(r_o/r_i).

questions.q: Put the transformed section steps for a two-material beam in order
steps: Scale each part's width by n = E_i/E_ref
Find the neutral axis and I_t of the transformed section
Compute σ = n M y / I_t in each material
questions.x: Scaling widths keeps the force carried at each depth, so the transformed section bends like a single material and n restores the true stress.

questions.q: Match each multi-material case to its behavior
pairs: Bonded layers loaded side by side
Equal strain, load shared in proportion to EA
Layers stacked end to end along the load
Strain linear through depth, stress jumps at the interface
Curves with the higher α material on the convex side
questions.x: Parallel arrangements share strain, series arrangements share stress, and a bonded interface keeps strain continuous while the modulus step makes stress jump.

questions.q: Uniform column clamped at one end and pinned at the other (k² = P/EI). Characteristic equation and P_cr?
questions.x: The lowest root kL ≈ 4.493 gives P_cr ≈ 20.19 EI/L² ≈ 2.05 π²EI/L², an effective length factor near 0.7.

questions.q: A column has different moments of inertia and end restraints in its two principal planes. It buckles in the plane with:
w: The strong axis, which carries more moment
The plane through the shear center
questions.x: Each plane has σ_cr = π²E/(KL/r)², so the plane with the largest effective slenderness has the lowest critical load and governs.

questions.q: Inelastic column buckling: tangent modulus load P_t, reduced modulus load P_r, actual maximum P_max. Shanley's result?
questions.a: Bending starts at P_t, and P_t ≤ P_max < P_r
w: Bending starts at P_r, and P_max = P_r
Bending starts at the Euler load with elastic E
questions.x: A column can begin to bend at the tangent modulus load while the load still rises, so P_t is the practical, slightly conservative design value.

questions.q: The Rayleigh quotient for column buckling, using any trial shape that meets the geometric boundary conditions, gives:
questions.a: An upper bound on the lowest P_cr
w: A lower bound on the lowest P_cr
The exact P_cr for every admissible shape
The mean of the first two critical loads
questions.x: An admissible shape adds artificial constraint, so its quotient ∫EI(w'')²dx/∫(w')²dx sits at or above the true lowest P_cr, with equality for the exact mode.

questions.q: Steel cantilever (flagpole) column: E = 200 GPa, I = 10⁶ mm⁴, L = 2000 mm. Euler critical load in kN (1 decimal)?
questions.x: Fixed-free has K = 2, so P_cr = π²EI/(4L²) = π²(2×10¹¹)/(1.6×10⁷) N ≈ 123.4 kN.

questions.q: Complete the elastic critical stress of a column
questions.x: Dividing P_cr = π²EI/(KL)² by A with I = Ar² gives σ_cr = π²E/(KL/r)², set by the slenderness ratio.

questions.q: Match each column end condition to its effective length factor K
questions.x: K is the distance between inflection points of the buckled shape divided by L, and P_cr = π²EI/(KL)².

questions.q: A tubular column of fixed cross-sectional area is redesigned with a larger diameter and thinner wall. Euler load rises until:
w: The Euler load starts to fall with diameter
Torsional buckling of the closed tube governs
The slenderness ratio exceeds the Johnson transition
questions.x: Spreading the same area outward raises r and the Euler load, while the local shell buckling stress scales with Et/R and drops, so the best design balances the two modes.
